title: How Theo built an audience and create-t3-app: Twitter for discovery, YouTube for conversion
summary: Theo explains the creator funnel (Twitter to discover, YouTube to succeed, Twitch to convert), why persistence beats single viral posts, and how one stack video became create-t3-app, built by community maintainers. He also covers opinionated-but-modular tooling and why community fills a mentorship gap.

principles.text: Match each platform to its funnel role: Twitter discovers, YouTube grows you, Twitch converts committed fans.
principles.quote: youtube is the place to succeed as a creator twitter's the place to get discovered

principles.text: Platforms with many encounters per session are best for finding an audience; bottom-funnel platforms only serve people who already know you.
principles.quote: nobody's going to twitch to find their next favorite streamer they're going there to follow the person that they met at the top of the funnel

principles.text: Followers come from persistence: people follow after seeing many good posts, not the first one.
principles.quote: nobody clicks the follow the first time you have a good tweet they click the follow when this is the 20th good tweet of yours they've seen

principles.text: Effort and payoff differ by platform: low-effort one-liners can blow up on Twitter, while YouTube demands heavy packaging like thumbnails and titles.
principles.quote: twitter is like low effort high discovery youtube is insanely high effort medium discovery decent conversion

principles.text: Know where your product's buyers actually are; streamers don't watch streams, so streaming a creator tool converts poorly even if viewers love it.
principles.quote: streamers don't watch streams and that's a really important thing to know

principles.text: Force users to make the decisions that matter instead of hiding them behind defaults, and comment the code heavily.
principles.quote: now we force you to think about it because those are decisions you have to make
